title: Digital Alternatives for Sports Clubs
overview: When in-person activity is not possible, sports clubs can use digital alternatives to stay connected, active, and supportive by moving training online. Live-streamed or recorded training sessions allow coaches to guide members at home, while simple fitness challenges, skill drills, or activity tracking help maintain motivation and routine. Regular communication through club apps, social media, or messaging platforms keeps members informed and connected, and virtual team meetings or social events help preserve a sense of belonging. By using accessible digital tools in a flexible and inclusive way, clubs can continue to support physical activity, wellbeing, and club culture even during periods of restriction.
guidelines: Start using digital communication tools in normal times so that staff and participants are already familiar with the tool when a crisis occurs
Use existing digital tools that are intuitive and/or that people are already familiar with

Find one or multiple digital tools for everyday informal communication (to motivate and create community, e.g., sending updates, photos, and messages) and live meetings or training sessions (to create moments together and give structure, e.g., video conferencing)
Create a digital communication space where people can easily share thoughts and updates
Make sure the tools you use are mobile-friendly and free for participants to use
Check in on participants individually who are not engaging
Set fun challenges, with a focus on effort and participation over performance
Propose set days or times for activity to help provide structure during times of uncertainty
Create clear expectations of what training participants should do and how they should engage through digital communication tools

Take steps to ensure the safety and privacy of individuals and their data. For example, use a tool that does not show participants each other's phone numbers if necessary. Make sure video links are not publicly accessible.
Designate someone in your team to provide technical support to staff and participants to avoid frustration, exclusion, or disengagement.
cooperation_guidance: Speak to other sport clubs and organisations to find out which digital tools they recommend.
Use digital communication tools now so that participants and staff are already familiar with them when you may become dependent on them.
Many digital tools are free, or provide discounts for charities and clubs, it may be beneficial to make contact with the provider(s) of the digital tool to find out what your options are.

case_example.context: During the COVID-19 pandemic from 2020, a running club in Brussels for young refugees used the Strava app to create a group and allow everyone to engage with new challenges, to follow each other's training, and to continue to feel part of a team.
key_approaches: We use a private Strava club to help young refugees in Brussels see each other’s runs, give kudos, and feel connected during the COVID-19 pandemic.
We set simple challenges to encourage regular participation and routine when group training was not possible.
We celebrate effort, consistency, and personal milestones to keep motivation high during periods of restriction and isolation.
We share routes, ideas, and suggested sessions around Brussels to inspire each other when running alone.
We use agreed virtual run days so participants feel they are running together, even when apart.
case_example.outcome: This approach helped us stay motivated, engaged, and connected despite lockdowns and the lack of in-person activity.
case_example.quote: [During the pandemic], since we weren’t allowed to run in group anymore, we created a 50 km challenge: everyone ran individually and tried to complete 50 km during December 2020. Every time you went for a run, you either sent a photo in WhatsApp or posted it on Strava.
